### Scaffold project with tiged

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/index.md

Create a local copy of a community template hosted on GitHub. Installs dependencies and starts the development server.

```bash
npx tiged user/project my-project
cd my-project

npm install
npm run dev
```

```bash
$ npm install # or pnpm install or yarn install
```

### Configure npm build and preview scripts in package.json

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/static-deploy.md

Add these npm scripts to package.json so the static deployment guides' commands work. Vite must be installed as a local dev dependency; `vite preview` is only for previewing the build locally, not a production server.

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "build": "vite build",
    "preview": "vite preview"
  }
}
```

### Create and start a Vite dev server with createServer

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/api-javascript.md

Initializes, starts, and prints URLs for a Vite development server programmatically with custom port and root configurations.

```ts
import { createServer } from 'vite'

const server = await createServer({
  // any valid user config options, plus `mode` and `configFile`
  configFile: false,
  root: import.meta.dirname,
  server: {
    port: 1337,
  },
})
await server.listen()

server.printUrls()
server.bindCLIShortcuts({ print: true })
```

### configurePreviewServer

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/api-plugin.md

Configures the Vite preview server instance. Called before internal middlewares are installed, with support for returning a post-hook callback to install middlewares afterward.

```APIDOC
### configurePreviewServer

#### Signature
`(server: PreviewServer) => (() => void) | void | Promise<(() => void) | void>`

#### Parameters
- `server` (`PreviewServer`) - The preview server instance.

#### Returns
- `(() => void) | void | Promise<(() => void) | void>` - Optionally returns a function called after internal middlewares are installed.

#### Details
- **Kind:** `async`, `sequential`
- **Scope:** Global
- Hook is called before other middlewares are installed. Return a post hook callback function if middleware should be injected after internal middlewares.

#### Example
```js
const myPlugin = () => ({
  name: 'configure-preview-server',
  configurePreviewServer(server) {
    // return a post hook that is called after other middlewares are installed
    return () => {
      server.middlewares.use((req, res, next) => {
        // custom handle request...
      })
    }
  },
})
```
```

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

Run in Vite's root folder to start the documentation site. Requires the types generated by pnpm run build for twoslash to work.

```shell
pnpm run docs
```

### Configure preview server port via --port in package.json

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/static-deploy.md

Pass the `--port` flag to change the preview server port; this example launches the server at `http://localhost:8080`.

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "preview": "vite preview --port 8080"
  }
}
```

### Run vite preview to locally preview the production build

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/cli.md

Starts a server in the build directory (default dist) to preview the production build. Run vite build beforehand to ensure the build directory is up-to-date. Do not use as a production server.

```bash
vite preview [root]
```

### HTML tags for entry point views/foo.js

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/backend-integration.md

Example of the tags to include in production for the entry point views/foo.js, following the recommended order for optimal performance.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="assets/foo-5UjPuW-k.css" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="assets/shared-ChJ_j-JJ.css" />
<script type="module" src="assets/foo-BRBmoGS9.js"></script>
<!-- optional -->
<link rel="modulepreload" href="assets/shared-B7PI925R.js" />
```

### Init function returns WebAssembly.Instance

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/playground/wasm/index.html

Checks that the init function returns a WebAssembly.Instance. The result is displayed as a boolean.

```javascript
import light from './light.wasm?init'

document
  .querySelector('.init-returns-instance .run')
  .addEventListener('click', async () => {
    const res = await light({
      imports: {
        imported_func: (res) => (resultElement.textContent = res),
      },
    })
    text(
      '.init-returns-instance .result',
      res instanceof WebAssembly.Instance,
    )
  })
```

### GitHub Pages deploy workflow for Vite

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/static-deploy.md

Sample `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` that installs dependencies with npm, builds the site, and deploys to GitHub Pages on pushes to `main`. Requires GitHub Pages source set to GitHub Actions.

```yaml
# Simple workflow for deploying static content to GitHub Pages
name: Deploy static content to Pages

on:
  # Runs on pushes targeting the default branch
  push:
    branches: ['main']

  # Allows you to run this workflow manually from the Actions tab
  workflow_dispatch:

# Sets the GITHUB_TOKEN permissions to allow deployment to GitHub Pages
permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Allow one concurrent deployment
concurrency:
  group: 'pages'
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # Single deploy job since we're just deploying
  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7
        with:
          node-version: lts/*
          cache: 'npm'
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci
      - name: Build
        run: npm run build
      - name: Setup Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@45bfe0192ca1faeb007ade9deae92b16b8254a0d # v6
      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@fc324d3547104276b827a68afc52ff2a11cc49c9 # v5
        with:
          # Upload dist folder
          path: './dist'
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@368f82528645a54fb793d4d04e342629a3f51346 # v5
```

### Output wasm init and run

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/playground/wasm/index.html

Uses the ?init import to instantiate an output wasm module. The testWasm function calls the init function with imports and then invokes the exported function.

```javascript
import heavy from './heavy.wasm?init'

async function testWasm(init, resultElement) {
  const { exported_func } = await init({
    imports: {
      imported_func: (res) => (resultElement.textContent = res),
    },
  }).then((i) => i.exports)
  exported_func()
}

document
  .querySelector('.output-wasm .run')
  .addEventListener('click', async () =>
    testWasm(heavy, document.querySelector('.output-wasm .result')),
  )
```

### Start Vite with native config loader

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/config/index.md

Executes the original config file directly so breakpoints in the config file and plugin hooks map to the original source. Requires a runtime supporting the syntax used, such as Node.js 22.18+ for TypeScript files.

```bash
vite --configLoader native
```

### Source phase import

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/playground/wasm/index.html

Uses source phase import to import a wasm module and instantiate it. The result of the add function is displayed.

```javascript
import source addModule from './add.wasm'

;(async () => {
  const addInstance = await WebAssembly.instantiate(addModule)
  text('.source-phase-wasm .result', addInstance.exports.add(1, 2))
})()
```

--------------------------------

### Configure app build with builder.buildApp in vite.config.js

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/api-environment-frameworks.md

Use the `builder.buildApp` option to control how environments are built, for example to build them in parallel. The option receives the `ViteBuilder` instance and is responsible for building each environment.

```js
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

export default defineConfig({
  builder: {
    buildApp: async (builder) => {
      const environments = Object.values(builder.environments)
      await Promise.all(
        environments.map((environment) => builder.build(environment)),
      )
    },
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Customize logger with createLogger to filter warnings

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/config/shared-options.md

Use Vite's createLogger API to get the default logger and customize it, for example to filter out certain warnings. This example ignores empty CSS files warnings.

```ts
import { createLogger, defineConfig } from 'vite'

const logger = createLogger()
const loggerWarn = logger.warn

logger.warn = (msg, options) => {
  // Ignore empty CSS files warning
  if (msg.includes('vite:css') && msg.includes(' is empty')) return
  loggerWarn(msg, options)
}

export default defineConfig({
  customLogger: logger,
})
```

### Dynamic source phase import

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/playground/wasm/index.html

Uses dynamic source phase import to import a wasm module and instantiate it. The result of the add function is displayed.

```javascript
;(async () => {
  const dynamicModule = await import.source('./add.wasm')
  const dynamicInstance = await WebAssembly.instantiate(dynamicModule)
  text(
    '.source-phase-wasm-dynamic .result',
    dynamicInstance.exports.add(3, 4),
  )
})()
```

### Define text utility for DOM updates

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

This helper sets the textContent of the element matching the given selector. It is used by the ?raw import example to display the imported content.

```js
function text(el, text) {
  document.querySelector(el).textContent = text
}
```

```html
<p>Hello Vite!</p>
```

### Import from UTF-8 BOM file and deep import with Babel runtime

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/playground/resolve/index.html

Imports a message from a UTF-8 BOM file and uses a deep import from @babel/runtime to slice an iterable. Requires the utf8-bom package and @babel/runtime to be installed.

```javascript
import { msg as bomMsg } from './utf8-bom/main.js'
text('.utf8-bom', bomMsg)

// deep import
import slicedToArray from '@babel/runtime/helpers/esm/slicedToArray'
const iterable = (function* () {
  yield 2
  yield 4
  yield 6
  yield 8
})()
text('.deep-import', JSON.stringify(slicedToArray(iterable, 2)))
```

### Inline wasm init and run

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/playground/wasm/index.html

Uses the ?init import to instantiate an inline wasm module. The testWasm function calls the init function with imports and then invokes the exported function.

```javascript
import light from './light.wasm?init'

async function testWasm(init, resultElement) {
  const { exported_func } = await init({
    imports: {
      imported_func: (res) => (resultElement.textContent = res),
    },
  }).then((i) => i.exports)
  exported_func()
}

document
  .querySelector('.inline-wasm .run')
  .addEventListener('click', async () =>
    testWasm(light, document.querySelector('.inline-wasm .result')),
  )
```

--------------------------------

### Example .vite/manifest.json generated by vite build

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/backend-integration.md

After running vite build, a .vite/manifest.json file is generated alongside other asset files. It maps source files to their build outputs and dependencies.

```json
{
  "_shared-B7PI925R.js": {
    "file": "assets/shared-B7PI925R.js",
    "name": "shared",
    "css": ["assets/shared-ChJ_j-JJ.css"]
  },
  "_shared-ChJ_j-JJ.css": {
    "file": "assets/shared-ChJ_j-JJ.css",
    "src": "_shared-ChJ_j-JJ.css"
  },
  "logo.svg": {
    "file": "assets/logo-BuPIv-2h.svg",
    "src": "logo.svg"
  },
  "baz.js": {
    "file": "assets/baz-B2H3sXNv.js",
    "name": "baz",
    "src": "baz.js",
    "isDynamicEntry": true
  },
  "views/bar.js": {
    "file": "assets/bar-gkvgaI9m.js",
    "name": "bar",
    "src": "views/bar.js",
    "isEntry": true,
    "imports": ["_shared-B7PI925R.js"],
    "dynamicImports": ["baz.js"]
  },
  "views/foo.js": {
    "file": "assets/foo-BRBmoGS9.js",
    "name": "foo",
    "src": "views/foo.js",
    "isEntry": true,
    "imports": ["_shared-B7PI925R.js"],
    "css": ["assets/foo-5UjPuW-k.css"]
  }
}
```

### Implicit index resolving and dir vs file

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/playground/resolve/index.html

Imports from a directory with an implicit index and from a directory that has both a file and an index. Requires the corresponding local files.

```javascript
// implicit index resolving
import { foo } from './util'
text('.index', foo())

// implicit dir index vs. file
import { file } from './dir'
text('.dir-vs-file', file)
```

### Profile Vite dev server with --profile --open

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md

Starts the Vite dev server with the built-in Node.js inspector to create a CPU profile. After the app loads, press p to stop the inspector and q to stop the dev server. Generates vite-profile.cpuprofile in the root folder.

```bash
vite --profile --open
```

--------------------------------

### Render links and preload directives with hashed filenames

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/backend-integration.md

Example HTML template showing how to render stylesheet links, module script, and modulepreload directives using a manifest. The syntax is for explanation only; substitute with your server templating language. The importedChunks function is for illustration and isn't provided by Vite.

```html
<!-- if production -->

<!-- for cssFile of manifest[name].css -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/{{ cssFile }}" />

<!-- for chunk of importedChunks(manifest, name) -->
<!-- for cssFile of chunk.css -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/{{ cssFile }}" />

<script type="module" src="/{{ manifest[name].file }}"></script>

<!-- for chunk of importedChunks(manifest, name) -->
<link rel="modulepreload" href="/{{ chunk.file }}" />
```

### Import and initialize WebAssembly modules using ?init

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/blog/announcing-vite3.md

Import a WebAssembly file using the ?init query suffix and invoke the default export to instantiate the module.

```javascript
import init from './example.wasm?init'

init().then((instance) => {
  instance.exports.test()
})
```

### Override Vite with a local build using pnpm overrides

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

Use this in the root pnpm-workspace.yaml to link a locally built Vite package. Requires pnpm v10.5+ and the package must also be listed as a dependency in the root package.json. After adding the override, re-run pnpm install to link the package.

```yaml
# pnpm-workspace.yaml
overrides:
  vite: link:../path/to/vite/packages/vite
```

--------------------------------

### Run Vite in Debug Mode with --debug Option

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

Use the --debug option to enable debugging logs. For example, `vite --debug resolve` shows logs for the resolve scope. To see all debug logs, use `vite --debug *`, but be warned that it will be quite noisy.

```bash
vite --debug resolve
```

```bash
vite --debug *
```

--------------------------------

### Inspect transform times using vite --debug transform

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/performance.md

Example debug output when running Vite with transform debugging enabled. Inspecting these logs helps identify slow-to-transform files that contribute to request waterfalls.

```bash
vite:transform 28.72ms /@vite/client +1ms
vite:transform 62.95ms /src/components/BigComponent.vue +1ms
vite:transform 102.54ms /src/utils/big-utils.js +1ms
```

Builds the app; by default the output is placed in the `dist` folder, which can be deployed to any platform.

```bash
$ npm run build
```

--------------------------------

### Configure server.open with a specific pathname in Vite config

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/config/server-options.md

Set server.open to a string to automatically open the app in the browser at that URL pathname on server start. The BROWSER and BROWSER_ARGS environment variables can be set in the .env file to choose a specific browser and pass extra arguments.

```javascript
export default defineConfig({
  server: {
    open: '/docs/index.html',
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Access environments via server.environments

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/api-environment-instances.md

During dev, access available environments in a dev server using `server.environments`. Use `server.environments.client` to get the client environment and `server.environments.ssr.moduleGraph` to access the SSR module graph.

```js
// create the server, or get it from the configureServer hook
const server = await createServer(/* options */)

const clientEnvironment = server.environments.client
clientEnvironment.transformRequest(url)
console.log(server.environments.ssr.moduleGraph)
```

### Configure multiple HTML entry points for multi-page build

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/build.md

Specify multiple `.html` files as entry points in `vite.config.js` using `input` mappings.

```javascript
import { resolve } from 'node:path'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

export default defineConfig({
  input: {
    main: resolve(import.meta.dirname, 'index.html'),
    nested: resolve(import.meta.dirname, 'nested/index.html'),
  },
})
```

### Install terser for legacy minification

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/packages/plugin-legacy/README.md

Installs terser as a development dependency. Required for minification when using Vite versions older than 8.1.4 or when build.minify is explicitly set to 'terser'.

```sh
npm add -D terser
```

### Install CSS pre-processors

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/features.md

Install the required pre-processor packages for Sass, Less, and Stylus. `sass-embedded` is recommended for performance; use `sass` if the platform is not supported.

```bash
# .scss and .sass
npm add -D sass-embedded # recommended for performance
npm add -D sass # if the platform is not supported

# .less
npm add -D less

# .styl and .stylus
npm add -D stylus
```

--------------------------------

### Overview of .env file loading hierarchy

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/env-and-mode.md

Lists the standard .env filenames Vite loads depending on the current mode and local override status.

```text
.env                # loaded in all cases
.env.local          # loaded in all cases, ignored by git
.env.[mode]         # only loaded in specified mode
.env.[mode].local   # only loaded in specified mode, ignored by git
```

### Build for Staging Mode and Configure .env.staging

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/env-and-mode.md

Override the default build mode using the --mode flag and provide matching environment variables in .env.staging.

```bash
vite build --mode staging
```

```.env.staging
VITE_APP_TITLE=My App (staging)
```

### Configure middleware using configurePreviewServer

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/api-plugin.md

Injects custom middleware after internal middlewares are installed by returning a post hook function from configurePreviewServer.

```js
const myPlugin = () => ({
  name: 'configure-preview-server',
  configurePreviewServer(server) {
    // return a post hook that is called after other middlewares are
    // installed
    return () => {
      server.middlewares.use((req, res, next) => {
        // custom handle request...
      })
    }
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Instantiate and execute code using ModuleRunner

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/api-environment-runtimes.md

Demonstrates initializing a `ModuleRunner` with an RPC transport and `ESModulesEvaluator` before executing an entry-point module.

```javascript
import {
  ModuleRunner,
  ESModulesEvaluator,
  createNodeImportMeta,
} from 'vite/module-runner'
import { transport } from './rpc-implementation.js'

const moduleRunner = new ModuleRunner(
  {
    transport,
    createImportMeta: createNodeImportMeta, // if the module runner runs in Node.js
  },
  new ESModulesEvaluator(),
)

await moduleRunner.import('/src/entry-point.js')
```

### Inject post-middleware via configureServer hook

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/api-plugin.md

Return a function from configureServer to register custom middlewares that execute after internal middlewares are installed.

```javascript
const myPlugin = () => ({
  name: 'configure-server',
  configureServer(server) {
    // return a post hook that is called after internal middlewares are
    // installed
    return () => {
      server.middlewares.use((req, res, next) => {
        // custom handle request...
      })
    }
  },
})
```

### Configure build.lib for multiple entries in vite.config.js

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/build.md

Specify an object in `build.lib.entry` to support bundling multiple entry points for a library.

```js
import { resolve } from 'node:path'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

export default defineConfig({
  build: {
    lib: {
      entry: {
        'my-lib': resolve(import.meta.dirname, 'lib/main.js'),
        secondary: resolve(import.meta.dirname, 'lib/secondary.js'),
      },
      name: 'MyLib',
    },
    rolldownOptions: {
      // make sure to externalize deps that shouldn't be bundled
      // into your library
      external: ['vue'],
      output: {
        // Provide global variables to use in the UMD build
        // for externalized deps
        globals: {
          vue: 'Vue',
        },
      },
    },
  },
})
```

    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/my-lib.js",

    }
  }
}

### Configure type-aware lint rules in .oxlintrc.json

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/packages/create-vite/template-react-ts/README.md

Enables type-aware linting with the react, typescript, and oxc plugins in .oxlintrc.json for production applications after installing oxlint-tsgolint.

```json
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/oxlint/configuration_schema.json",
  "plugins": ["react", "typescript", "oxc"],
  "options": {
    "typeAware": true
  },
  "rules": {
    "react/rules-of-hooks": "error",
    "react/only-export-components": ["warn", { "allowConstantExport": true }]
  }
}
```

### createServer(inlineConfig?)

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/api-javascript.md

Creates a Vite development server instance programmatically. It accepts an optional configuration object and returns a promise resolving to a ViteDevServer.

```APIDOC
## createServer

### Description
Creates a Vite development server instance programmatically.

### Type Signature
```ts
async function createServer(inlineConfig?: InlineConfig): Promise<ViteDevServer>
```

### Parameters
- **inlineConfig** (`InlineConfig`, optional) - Any valid user configuration options, plus `mode` and `configFile`.

### Returns
- `Promise<ViteDevServer>` - Resolves to the created development server instance.

### Usage Example
```ts
import { createServer } from 'vite'

const server = await createServer({
  // any valid user config options, plus `mode` and `configFile`
  configFile: false,
  root: import.meta.dirname,
  server: {
    port: 1337,
  },
})
await server.listen()

server.printUrls()
server.bindCLIShortcuts({ print: true })
```

### Middleware Mode Example with WebSocket Proxy
```ts
import http from 'http'
import { createServer } from 'vite'

const parentServer = http.createServer() // or express, koa, etc.

const vite = await createServer({
  server: {
    // Enable middleware mode
    middlewareMode: {
      // Provide the parent http server for proxy WebSocket
      server: parentServer,
    },
    proxy: {
      '/ws': {
        target: 'ws://localhost:3000',
        // Proxying WebSocket
        ws: true,
      },
    },
  },
})

parentServer.use(vite.middlewares)
```
```

--------------------------------

### Pseudo implementation of importedChunks in TypeScript

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/backend-integration.md

Example TypeScript function to recursively collect imported chunks from a Vite manifest. Adapt for your programming and templating language.

```ts
import type { Manifest, ManifestChunk } from 'vite'

export default function importedChunks(
  manifest: Manifest,
  name: string,
): ManifestChunk[] {
  const seen = new Set<string>()

  function getImportedChunks(chunk: ManifestChunk): ManifestChunk[] {
    const chunks: ManifestChunk[] = []
    for (const file of chunk.imports ?? []) {
      const importee = manifest[file]
      if (seen.has(file)) {
        continue
      }
      seen.add(file)

      chunks.push(...getImportedChunks(importee))
      chunks.push(importee)
    }

    return chunks
  }

  return getImportedChunks(manifest[name])
}
```

--------------------------------

### Configure server.warmup in Vite

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/config/server-options.md

Use this to warm up files to transform and cache the results in advance, improving initial page load and preventing transform waterfalls. clientFiles are used in the client only, while ssrFiles are used in SSR only; both accept file paths or tinyglobby patterns relative to root. Only add frequently used files to avoid overloading the dev server on startup.

```js
export default defineConfig({
  server: {
    warmup: {
      clientFiles: ['./src/components/*.vue', './src/utils/big-utils.js'],
      ssrFiles: ['./src/server/modules/*.js'],
    },
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Configure default Vite npm scripts in package.json

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/index.md

Default npm scripts in a scaffolded Vite project for starting the dev server, building for production, and previewing the build locally.

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "vite", // start dev server, aliases: `vite dev`, `vite serve`
    "build": "vite build", // build for production
    "preview": "vite preview" // locally preview production build
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Configure basic experimental.renderBuiltUrl for runtime and relative URLs

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/build.md

Use `experimental.renderBuiltUrl` to customize asset URLs based on `hostType`, returning dynamic runtime expressions or relative paths.

```ts
import type { UserConfig } from 'vite'
// prettier-ignore
const config: UserConfig = {
// ---cut-before---
experimental: {
  renderBuiltUrl(filename, { hostType }) {
    if (hostType === 'js') {
      return { runtime: `window.__toCdnUrl(${JSON.stringify(filename)})` }
    } else {
      return { relative: true }
    }
  },
},
// ---cut-after---
}
```

### Worker wasm

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/playground/wasm/index.html

Imports a worker using the ?worker suffix and listens for messages. The worker's result is displayed in the element with class 'worker-wasm .result'.

```javascript
import myWorker from './worker?worker'

const w = new myWorker()
w.addEventListener('message', (ev) => {
  text('.worker-wasm .result', ev.data.result)
})
```

--------------------------------

### Typical SSR application source file structure

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/ssr.md

Shows the recommended directory and file layout for an SSR application, including server, universal code, client entry, and server entry files.

```text
- index.html
- server.js # main application server
- src/
  - main.js          # exports env-agnostic (universal) app code
  - entry-client.js  # mounts the app to a DOM element
  - entry-server.js  # renders the app using the framework's SSR API
```

### Installing and registering @vitejs/plugin-legacy

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/using-plugins.md

Add a plugin to devDependencies and include it in the plugins array inside vite.config.js. Vite accepts presets as nested arrays and automatically flattens them, ignoring any falsy plugin values.

```bash
$ npm add -D @vitejs/plugin-legacy
```

```javascript
import legacy from '@vitejs/plugin-legacy'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    legacy({
      targets: ['defaults', 'not IE 11'],
    }),
  ],
})
```

### Source phase import instantiated with imports

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/playground/wasm/index.html

Uses source phase import to import a wasm module that requires imports, then instantiates it with the provided imports. The result is displayed.

```javascript
import source lightWithImportsModule from './light-with-imports.wasm'
import { imported_func } from './imports.js'
import { getResult } from './imports.js'

;(async () => {
  const lwiInstance = await WebAssembly.instantiate(lightWithImportsModule, {
    './imports.js': {
      imported_func,
    },
  })
  lwiInstance.exports.exported_func()
  text('.source-phase-wasm-with-imports .result', getResult())
})()
```
